advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass an explicit `timeout=` to `urllib.request.urlopen` in `_download` so a stalled scanner download fails fast instead of hanging the lane/build.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:237: `with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response, dest.open("wb") as fh:` — no `timeout=` argument
urlopen defaults to no timeout (blocks forever on a stalled connection); this runs in `make scanner-integration` (Makefile) and the Dockerfile RUN step (infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:52)
advisory.finding: `_download` calls `urllib.request.urlopen(url)` with no timeout, so a hung or slow Gitleaks release download blocks the scanner-integration CI lane and the review-bot Docker build indefinitely (no fail-fast).
advisory.suggested_fix: with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response, dest.open("wb") as fh:

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject non-`https` schemes on `gitleaks_url` (and `checksums_url`) before calling `urllib.request.urlopen` in `_download`.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:237: `with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response, dest.open("wb") as fh:`
No scheme allow-list (e.g. require `https://`) is applied to `entry.gitleaks_url` before it reaches `urlopen`.
advisory.finding: `_download()` fetches the Gitleaks archive with `urllib.request.urlopen(url)` using the raw URL from the committed manifest without validating the URL scheme, so a manifest that sets a `file://` or `ftp://` URL would be honored. The digest check still runs afterward, but a `file://` URL pointed at an attacker-writable local path whose bytes match the pinned digest, or a non-HTTPS transport, is not blocked at the fetch layer.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a guard in `_download`/`_entry_from_manifest` that raises `ScannerInstallError` unless the URL parses to scheme `https`.
